summary: BA's structural-claim evidence (line numbers, file sizes, grep results) is verified accurate. Reference patterns (TaskView 33-54/97-121, ICON_TASK at knownTools:11, taskLikeTool 40-63, CronList 939-953, exec_command_begin 294-321) all check out empirically. Scope coverage of all 5 verbs + §5.13 closure + §5.7/§5.18 contract enforcement is complete. However, two material investigation gaps remain that put the implementation at risk of failure: (1) BA never confirmed that Codex actually emits `spawn_agent_begin/end`-style events at all — the `codexAppServerClient.ts` event surface (item/started/completed JSON-RPC) currently emits only `commandExecution`, `fileChange`, `agentMessage` item types. Adding sessionProtocolMapper.ts branches for events that do not exist in the upstream Codex stream will produce zero envelopes regardless of how clean the branches are. (2) The view-routing mechanism is `toolViewRegistry` in `views/_all.tsx`, NOT a `view:` field on knownTools entries — but `_all.tsx` is missing from the affected_files / files_to_modify list. Dev will likely discover this mid-implementation and either (a) add it ad-hoc without BA awareness, or (b) ship a CodexSubagentView that is never actually mounted. These are FAIL-grade gaps, not nitpicks.

scope_gap.issue: BA does not list `packages/happy-app/sources/components/tools/views/_all.tsx` as an affected file
scope_gap.rationale: The view-routing mechanism in this codebase is `toolViewRegistry: Record<string, ToolViewComponent>` exported from `views/_all.tsx` (lines 33-50). To wire CodexSubagentView for the 5 verbs, dev MUST add 5 entries to that registry mapping each `functions.spawn_agent` etc. to `CodexSubagentView`. The BA `Affected files` list (lines 152-156) and context JSON `affected_files` (3 items) and `files_to_modify` (2 items) all OMIT _all.tsx. The BA does mention 'CodexSubagentView view routing' as an Edge Case (line 116) and instructs dev to 'verify the routing convention ... use the CodexPatchView or TaskView wiring as reference', but stops short of explicitly enumerating _all.tsx as a file to modify. Risk: dev could ship a knownTools entry referencing a view component that is never registered, resulting in either silent fallback to default rendering or a missed wiring step found only at QA time.

issues.issue: Codex event names for spawn_agent_begin/end etc. are HYPOTHESIZED, not verified empirically
issues.evidence: BA spec line 78 (R7) says: 'event naming convention TBD by Dev reading existing Codex event stream; likely `spawn_agent_begin`/`spawn_agent_end` etc., following `exec_command_begin/end` convention'. BA spec line 112 (Edge Cases) acknowledges: 'they may use a unified `function_call_begin`/`function_call_end` with a `name` field. Dev must read the actual Codex event stream or the codex processor types before implementing the mapper branches. If names are uncertain, add a comment with the assumption.' QA's empirical check of `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts` lines 280-340 shows the Codex event surface is a JSON-RPC `method === 'item/started' / 'item/completed'` stream where `item.type` is one of `commandExecution`, `fileChange`, `agentMessage` (lines 280, 309, 342). NO existing branch handles a subagent / spawn / delegate item type. NO existing event type emits a `_begin/_end` for any function call other than exec_command and patch_apply. Adding sessionProtocolMapper.ts branches for `spawn_agent_begin` will be inert if the Codex runtime does not emit that event type. The actual mechanism may require: (a) handling a NEW item.type value in codexAppServerClient.ts FIRST, OR (b) intercepting tool-call records from `agent_message`/turn diff payloads, OR (c) the Codex runtime simply does not surface these as discrete events. None of these alternatives were investigated.

objections.title: Codex event-stream existence is hypothesized, not verified
objections.detail: BA spec R7 (line 78) and AC5 (line 140) prescribe adding sessionProtocolMapper.ts branches for `spawn_agent_begin/end`, `send_input_begin/end`, etc. QA empirical check of the upstream Codex event surface (codexAppServerClient.ts:280-340) shows the event handler dispatches on `method === 'item/started' / 'item/completed'` with `item.type` ∈ {`commandExecution`, `fileChange`, `agentMessage`}. There is no existing precedent for any subagent or function-call item type. The BA's 'event naming TBD' hedge is insufficient — BA could and should have grep'd codexAppServerClient.ts and codex's TS types to confirm whether ANY event mechanism exists for these 5 verbs at the protocol level. If Codex does not emit subagent events at all, the entire mapper-side workstream (R7 / AC5) is moot and the implementation fails its acceptance criterion silently.
objections.required_action: Before dev starts, BA (or dev as part of investigation) must Grep `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerTypes.ts` and `codexAppServerClient.ts` for ANY mention of `spawn`, `subagent`, `delegate`, `wait_agent`, `function_call`, `tool_call` to determine: (a) whether the events exist under names BA didn't anticipate, (b) whether they require new item.type cases in codexAppServerClient.ts, or (c) whether the runtime simply does not emit them. Document the finding and revise R7 accordingly. If the events do not exist, the spec must be downgraded to 'app-side only' (knownTools entries + CodexSubagentView) and §5.13 cannot be closed by this pipeline.

verdict_rationale: The BA's structural evidence is strong — every line-number / line-count / grep claim reproduces. Scope coverage is comprehensive: all 5 verbs, §5.13 closure, §5.7/§5.18 contracts, and the 'one shared view' constraint are all captured. However, the spec has TWO investigation gaps that will block dev from delivering a working result: (1) the Codex event types `spawn_agent_begin/end` etc. are unverified and may not exist at all in the upstream event stream — making R7 / AC5 potentially undeliverable; (2) the view-routing file `views/_all.tsx` is not listed as an affected file, so dev's CodexSubagentView.tsx may ship without ever being mounted. These are FAIL-grade gaps because they will manifest as silent runtime failures (cards not rendering, envelopes never emitted) that look exactly like the symptom this spec is supposed to fix. Verdict: BA must revise the spec to either (a) add empirical verification of the Codex event surface and explicitly list _all.tsx as an affected file, or (b) downgrade the spec scope to app-side-only with a documented contingency for the protocol-side work.
